solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Copy type of smart card, getting glib about it

indicators.note: one word going about another wraps around it, so the card type sits inside the word for glib

parts.note: facile means superficially fluent, glib
a SIM card is the smart card in a mobile phone

explanation.surface: Someone forges a smart card while talking slickly to cover it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A facsimile is an exact reproduction of a document or object, so a copy.

clue.text: Flaubert's first clever story

indicators.note: first asks only for the opening letter of the novelist's name

parts.note: opening letter of Flaubert
able means capable, clever

explanation.surface: Praise for the French novelist's first clever tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable is a short tale, often with animals, carrying a moral.

clue.text: Downcast, emblem having dropped off wall?

parts.note: a heraldic crest is an emblem
something that has dropped off a wall has fallen

explanation.surface: A coat of arms has fallen off the wall, leaving the owner dejected.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the whimsy: read literally, the answer is a crest that has fallen.
explanation.definitionFit: Crestfallen means dejected and disappointed, as if one's plume had drooped.

clue.text: Animal smell appalling at first in pub

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the word for a pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
hum is British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: at first means just the start, so only the opening letter of appalling is taken

parts.note: opening letter of appalling

explanation.surface: An appalling animal stink hangs about a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal as an adjective means brutish or bestial, lacking human feeling, which is inhuman.

clue.text: One church sure to be inaccessible in winter?

parts.note: Roman numeral one
CE stands for the Church of England
bound to happen means sure to happen

explanation.surface: A church that is certain to be cut off once winter comes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: being frozen in is one winter way to be inaccessible.
explanation.definitionFit: Icebound means trapped or blocked by ice, so a place or ship that cannot be reached.

clue.text: Greek mathematician, 50, in Brussels police department

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old Greek mathematician turns up in a Brussels police department.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid was the ancient Greek geometer whose Elements founded classical geometry.

clue.text: Light shawl principally found in Central Manchuria

indicators.note: principally means at the start, so each of the next two words gives its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of found

indicators.note: central asks for the core of the place name, the letters at its very middle

parts.note: opening letter of in
the middle three of its nine letters

explanation.surface: A travel note about a delicate shawl mostly seen in the heart of Manchuria.
explanation.definitionFit: A fichu is a small triangular shawl worn round the shoulders and knotted at the breast, a lightweight wrap.

clue.text: Be unsuccessful catching insect? A pigeon?

indicators.note: catching means trapping, so the verb's letters close around the insect

parts.note: to fail is to be unsuccessful
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bird fails to catch an insect, prompting the query whether it is a pigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: The fantail is a fancy breed of domestic pigeon with a spread, fan-shaped tail.

clue.text: Vehicle needing a lot of attention

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: care means attention, as in take care

explanation.surface: An old banger of a vehicle that needs plenty of maintenance.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is a motor vehicle for carrying passengers on roads.

clue.text: International firm showing careless indifference

parts.note: the United Nations, the international body
a concern is a business

explanation.surface: A multinational company displays a casual lack of care.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconcern is a lack of worry or interest, an attitude of not caring.

clue.text: Drone, perhaps, initially caught high in tree

parts.note: a drone is a male bee, an example flagged by perhaps

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: opening letter of caught
H is the standard abbreviation for high

explanation.surface: A drone aircraft gets stuck high up in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Drone looks like the flying machine, but here it is the male honeybee.
explanation.definitionFit: The beech is a common broadleaf woodland species with smooth grey bark.

clue.text: Cranky chap touring cape with very little money

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the man's name travels around the other letters

parts.note: a typical man's name
C is the map abbreviation for cape
a cent is a coin of tiny value

explanation.surface: An irritable man goes round a headland with hardly any cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Cranky chap reads as one phrase, but only Cranky is the definition; chap is a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranky in its sense of odd or quirky describes someone unconventional in behaviour.

clue.text: Old flame playing for time, speaking off the cuff (with son, not unknown)

indicators.note: the letter standing for son takes the place of the one used for an unknown in algebra

parts.note: a former partner
temporising is stalling to gain time
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A former lover stalls for time while talking unprepared.
explanation.walkthrough: Unknown is Z, a letter used for an algebra variable; swapping it for S turns the -ize spelling into the -ise one.
explanation.definitionFit: Extemporisation is improvisation, talking or performing without preparation, which is what off the cuff means.

clue.text: Unflinching Catholic dignitary holding up in current board

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece that holds another up sits beneath it, so the dignitary comes after the next word

parts.note: taken as written
Dom is a title for some Catholic monks and abbots
I is the symbol for electric current
board as in a table for food

explanation.surface: A steadfast churchman shores things up on the current board.
explanation.walkthrough: Dom is the honorific for Benedictine and other monastic superiors. In a down answer, one piece holding up another sits directly below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Indomitable means impossible to subdue, so someone who never flinches or gives way.

clue.text: Liberal in criticising local government procedure

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the word that follows it

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal councillor attacks how the council runs things.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain planning is the council process that grants or refuses permission to build.
explanation.definitionFit: Planning control is a core function of local councils, deciding building and land-use applications.

clue.text: Old college principal rejecting a painter's many-sided figures

parts.note: a polytechnic, an old kind of British college

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing out, so the single letter named is taken away

parts.note: the head of a school
taken as written
RA, Royal Academician, a painter; 's is is

explanation.surface: A former college head rejects an artist's drawings of complex shapes.
explanation.walkthrough: Polytechnics were British colleges that became universities in 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyhedra are solid figures bounded by many flat faces, the plural of polyhedron.

clue.text: Promise offered by place to est of border

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
an edge is a border or margin

explanation.surface: A pledge offered by a place lying on the far side of a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The source text reads est, apparently west with its first letter lost: in an across answer place sits west, to the left, of border.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn undertaking, so a noun synonym for a promise.

clue.text: Disallow simple song, mostly one for robbers

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the word for a song loses its final letter

parts.note: to ban is to forbid
a ditty is a short simple song
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Banning a simple tune seems a job for robbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditti is the old Italian plural of bandit, outlaws who rob travellers.

clue.text: Flop about, laughing out loud before cut

parts.note: the texting abbreviation
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: Someone collapses in fits of laughter before being cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to move in an ungainly bounding or flopping way, like a big dog.

clue.text: Take too much time with respect to trip

parts.note: over as in arguing over, regarding
a run is a short journey

explanation.surface: A journey that took longer than planned.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to go beyond the allotted time, as a meeting does.

clue.text: Skipper of boat identity theft knocked back!

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so the two words are read from the end

parts.note: a name identifies someone
a grab is a snatch, a theft

explanation.surface: A boat captain has their identity stolen, and it is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargeman works and steers a barge, so he is in charge of that boat.

clue.text: Plant Asquith, say, endlessly encountered in Georgia

indicators.note: encountered in means found inside, so the trimmed name goes within the abbreviation
endlessly means without ends, so the name loses its first and last letters

parts.note: GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia
H. H. Asquith, the British Prime Minister, was named Herbert

explanation.surface: A plant in Georgia is named after the former Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Asquith, say gives a first name by example: Herbert Henry Asquith led Britain 1908 to 1916.
explanation.definitionFit: The gerbera is a daisy-like flowering plant, popular as a cut flower.

clue.text: Writer crossing a road, like certain poets

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the pen name spans the other letters

parts.note: a Bic is a ballpoint pen, a writer
A plus RD, the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A writer crossing a road is likened to certain poets.
explanation.walkthrough: Writer suggests an author, but here it is the pen brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Bardic describes bards, the ancient Celtic poet-singers, so it suits poets of that kind.

clue.text: In England her tales involved two fairy-tale siblings

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these words are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An English storyteller's tales feature a famous brother and sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Hansel and Gretel are the brother and sister of the Grimm tale who meet the witch in the gingerbread house.

clue.text: Large vehicle runs into small parrot

indicators.note: running into means going inside, so the letter enters the bird's name

parts.note: a lory is a small brightly coloured parrot
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A truck hits a little parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: A lorry is the British word for a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorry is a big goods vehicle, called a truck in America.

clue.text: Cast doubt on record right to prepare for publishing

parts.note: a gramophone record
R is the abbreviation for right
editing readies text for print

explanation.surface: Someone questions whether a record is fit to be edited for print.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit a claim is to make it seem false, which casts doubt upon it.

clue.text: In folk-tales, a wicked gnome

indicators.note: In means contained within, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the a, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: In folk tales there is often a wicked gnome.
explanation.walkthrough: The gnome is not the garden creature: gnome also means a pithy saying or maxim.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb, and a gnome is likewise a short aphorism.

clue.text: Subscriber loses head, seeing glowing coal

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a subscriber to a club or society is a member

explanation.surface: A subscriber is beheaded at the sight of a hot coal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a small piece of burning or smouldering coal left in a dying fire.

clue.text: Egyptian town with a hospital on the outskirts

indicators.note: being on the outskirts means surrounding, so the hospital phrase forms a ring round the single letter

parts.note: A plus SAN, short for sanatorium
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: An Egyptian town that has a hospital on its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Aswan is a city on the Nile in southern Egypt, famous for its dams.

clue.text: Lines by stylish woman dismissing knight's sharp practice

parts.note: chic means elegant

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the letter for a chess knight is removed from the woman's name

parts.note: a woman's name
N is the chess notation for knight
RY is short for railway, lines of track

explanation.surface: A fashionable woman's lines that dismiss a knight sound like trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines comes first in the clue, but by puts it after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicanery is trickery or deception, the underhand dealing that sharp practice describes.
